Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, ses…

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"


  teammate:
    needs: dedupe
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; the
    # pr_approved label re-entry (merge bot arming) and dispatch runs (SM /
    # manual leg override) reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
       github.event.issue.pull_request == null) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      # Toolchains the agent legs install (cached). Unlisted = nothing installed.
      flutter-version: 'stable'
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME: 'ZAI_API_KEY'
    # Explicit mapping — see the secrets note at the top of this file.
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group
# — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow (it
# waits forever on a group its own caller holds).
#
# Agent code and the dmtools CLI are NOT tied to the workflow pin: they
# resolve from RELEASES at run time by repo variables (bump = repo-settings
# edit, zero workflow changes):
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools (Java) CLI release tag ('latest' default)
name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main (same pin as ai-teammate.yml).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # #687: whose login is "the machine" — pr_approved arming and the
      # auto-rework rules fire only on PRs authored by this login
      # (.dmtools/config.js machineAuthor carries the same value).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the required
      # protection check itself. your branch protection requires
      # exactly these contexts; keep the names in sync with the ruleset.
      validation-checks: '["test"]'
      # sm_github.json validation rules dispatch THIS repo's PR CI
      # (unit-tests.yml) on PR heads — without it the required context
      # never appears and approved PRs stall BLOCKED.
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified); it rides
      # this INPUT instead.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time. EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares.
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token).
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic merge bot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # your PR CI — the bot's workflow-run fallback reads its runs when
      # a head carries no check runs.
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Now let me look at the repository structure, the other workflows (ci.yml), FORK_E2E_MARKER.md, and the instruction.md file mentioned in guidelines. Let me also check the outputs dir and .dmtools config.

Key review questions for this PR:

1. **The change**: All reusable workflow `uses:` refs repointed from `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` to `ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows@main`. Plus an added `issue_comment: types: [created]` trigger in ai-teammate.yml, with a guard `github.event.issue.pull_request == null` so only issue (non-PR) comments re-arm the dev leg.

2. **Security considerations**:
  - Pining: The workflows now point at `@main` of a FORK. The comments in machine-sm.yml say "pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main (same pin as ai-teammate.yml)" — but the actual ref is `@main`, not an immutable SHA. That's a stale comment, and also a security consideration: reusable workflow refs at `@main` are mutable — a compromise of the fork allows arbitrary workflow execution with broad permissions (contents: write, issues: write, pull-requests: write, actions: write). This is a supply-chain concern. However, note the PR description says the fork wiring is intentional (self-hosted fork loop). Prior state already used @main (of IstiN). So the mutable-ref risk is pre-existing, not introduced. But the comments are now stale/inconsistent (they say pinned to immutable SHA but ref is @main).
  - The `issue_comment` trigger + guard: `github.event.issue.pull_request == null` filters PR comments. Issue comments on ANY issue (not just needs-input ones) will trigger a run — but the factory guard presumably filters. This creates a potential run-amplification vector: any repo member commenting on any issue triggers a workflow run that consumes AI provider credits (ZAI_API_KEY). Hmm — but that's the design (comment-resume). The dedupe job handles twins. Also note: comments on issues not assigned to ai-teammate... the guard lets ALL issue comments through to the factory. Does the factory gate filter on assignment? We can't see the factory internals (external repo). The `if` condition for issue_comment only checks `pull_request == null`, NOT assignment to ai-teammate, and not label presence. So ANY comment on ANY issue (including ones unrelated to the machine) arms a run of the factory workflow, which will call the LM provider. That's a cost/security consideration. But is it blocking? The factory itself presumably has a guard (the comment says "comment-resume; PR comments are filtered by the if below"). The factory gate (mentioned in comment "re-arm the dev leg via the factory gate") may filter to needs-input issues. Since we can't verify the factory internals, this is worth an IMPORTANT note: the stub-level guard allows every non-PR issue comment to reach the factory — potential cost amplification / unintended runs on unrelated issues. Actually wait — let me think about whether that's true. The `if` on the teammate job: for issue_comment events, only `github.event.issue.pull_request == null` is required. So yes, any issue comment triggers. But also `needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'` — dedupe only cancels when another live run holds the same anchor. So every comment on any issue starts a factory run (subject to concurrency serialization per issue). The factory gate may no-op it (the comment says "re-arm the dev leg via the factory gate (comment-resume)"). The design intent is that the factory decides. This matches "Content identical to ai/gh-2's workflow wiring" — the referenced gh-2 workflow wiring in the ai branch. Hmm.

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

          node --check .dmtools/config.js

        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:

🚨 **⚠️ IMPORTANT: "immutable SHA" pin claim vs mutable `@main` ref**

The comment above this line (lines 44–45) still says the loop is *"pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main (same pin as ai-teammate.yml)"* — but the actual ref is the **mutable `@main` of the `ajaxspace` fork**, and the same mutable-ref pattern now applies to **all five stubs** (`ai-teammate.yml:138`, `machine-merge.yml:40`, `machine-sm.yml:46`, `merge-trigger.yml:29`, `sm-kicker.yml:39`).

Why this matters more than a stale comment: these calls carry a `contents: write / actions: write / issues: write / pull-requests: write` ceiling (`ai-teammate.yml`), `machine-sm.yml` passes `silent-token: ${{ github.token }}`, and `merge-trigger.yml` uses `secrets: inherit`. Whoever can push to `ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows@main` can execute arbitrary workflow code inside this repo. Same-owner fork keeps the trust boundary at "repo admins", but the current comments assert a pin that does not exist.

Suggested options (either is fine):

1. Pin by full commit SHA (current fork main, verified this run):
   ```yaml
   uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@d0c672e5df4f4190c854ae7330239718dc059bd6  # fork main @ comment-resume (#2)
   ```
   (bump = one-line commit; the agents/dmtools versions already ride `vars.AGENTS_VERSION`/`vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION` from RELEASES, so freezing the workflow ref does not freeze the toolchain)
2. Or correct the comments to say `@main` (mutable, fork-as-release-channel) so the docs match reality.

Not blocking: the mutable-`@main` pattern is pre-existing (previously `IstiN/...@main`), and fork-main-as-release-channel is the documented self-hosting design; this is hardening + doc-accuracy debt, worth fixing in this PR since the lines are touched anyway.

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard passes every comment on every issue — document the breadth (no change required)**

The added filter (`github.event.issue.pull_request == null`) correctly drops PR comments, but stub-side there is **no assignee/label filter** for `issue_comment`: a comment on *any* issue — not just `ai-teammate`-assigned or `needs-input` tickets — passes this guard and starts a run, and the factory gate (`comment-resume`, verified present on fork `main` as `EVENT_NAME`/`COMMENT_AUTHOR`/`COMMENT_ID` in the guard env) is the only thing that decides whether it re-arms a dev leg. That's bounded (per-issue concurrency, `cancel-in-progress: false`) and matches the documented design, so no change is strictly needed.

Two behavioral notes worth knowing:

- **First-wins vs. mid-run replies**: while a dev leg is live on issue N, `dedupe` self-cancels any comment-triggered run for N (it appears in the `queued`/`pending` scan). A human reply landing *during* a run therefore re-arms nothing — the author must re-comment after the leg ends. Fine for the needs-input flow (the leg ends with the question before the human replies), but surprising if a reply arrives while the agent is still working.
- **Cost**: each `created` comment on an open issue costs one runner spin-up + factory-guard execution even when the gate no-ops it. If that ever gets noisy, an additional stub-side condition (e.g. issue assigned to `ai-teammate`) would pre-filter cheaply — the factory gate stays the source of truth either way.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, ses…

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"


  teammate:
    needs: dedupe
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; the
    # pr_approved label re-entry (merge bot arming) and dispatch runs (SM /
    # manual leg override) reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
       github.event.issue.pull_request == null) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      # Toolchains the agent legs install (cached). Unlisted = nothing installed.
      flutter-version: 'stable'
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME: 'ZAI_API_KEY'
    # Explicit mapping — see the secrets note at the top of this file.
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtoo…

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group
# — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow (it
# waits forever on a group its own caller holds).
#
# Agent code and the dmtools CLI are NOT tied to the workflow pin: they
# resolve from RELEASES at run time by repo variables (bump = repo-settings
# edit, zero workflow changes):
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools (Java) CLI release tag ('latest' default)
name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main (same pin as ai-teammate.yml).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # #687: whose login is "the machine" — pr_approved arming and the
      # auto-rework rules fire only on PRs authored by this login
      # (.dmtools/config.js machineAuthor carries the same value).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the required
      # protection check itself. your branch protection requires
      # exactly these contexts; keep the names in sync with the ruleset.
      validation-checks: '["test"]'
      # sm_github.json validation rules dispatch THIS repo's PR CI
      # (unit-tests.yml) on PR heads — without it the required context
      # never appears and approved PRs stall BLOCKED.
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified); it rides
      # this INPUT instead.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time. EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares.
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token).
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic merge bot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # your PR CI — the bot's workflow-run fallback reads its runs when
      # a head carries no check runs.
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# All logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-merge-trigger.yml; the event triggers stay repo-side
# (workflow_run on Unit Tests + issues:labeled re-entry — the label event
# must not be swallowed when CI hasn't run yet).
name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : Unit Tests passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge-trigger.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      remove_pr_label: true
      map_pr_labels: true
      gh_branch_pattern: true
    # `secrets: inherit` is safe here — the factory-merge-trigger declares
    # NO `secrets:` block under workflow_call, so required-secret
    # validation cannot fail at startup; explicitly mapping an UNdeclared
    # secret is rejected at call time.
    secrets: inherit

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Why this repo needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet
# repos — the kicker re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule +
# every non-main push, so the state machine keeps moving even when the
# machine-sm cron is dropped.
#
# Event-driven wake-up: validation verdicts arrive as CI
# conclusions (your PR CI workflow);
# reacting to them closes the gap — latch/merge happens within seconds of
# the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: 'CI'
      # The required protection context is the single `test` job named
      # "Java unit tests" ("Protect main" ruleset — see unit-tests.yml).
      required_contexts: 'test'

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY

The added filter (`github.event.issue.pull_request == null`) correctly drops PR comments, but stub-side there is **no assignee/label filter** for `issue_comment`: a comment on *any* issue — not just `ai-teammate`-assigned or `needs-input` tickets — passes this guard and starts a run, and the factory gate (`comment-resume`, verified present on fork `main` as `EVENT_NAME`/`COMMENT_AUTHOR`/`COMMENT_ID` in the guard env) is the only thing that decides whether it re-arms a dev leg. Two behavioral notes worth knowing:

- **First-wins vs. mid-run replies**: while a dev leg is live on issue N, `dedupe` self-cancels any comment-triggered run for N (it appears in the `queued`/`pending` scan). A human reply landing *during* a run therefore re-arms nothing — the author must re-comment after the leg ends. Fine for the needs-input flow (the leg ends with the question before the human replies), but surprising if a reply arrives while the agent is still working.
- **Cost**: each `created` comment on an open issue costs one runner spin-up + factory-guard execution even when the gate no-ops it. If that ever gets noisy, an additional stub-side condition (e.g. issue assigned to `ai-teammate`) would pre-filter cheaply — the factory gate stays the source of truth either way.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, ses…

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'

                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')

            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true

    if: >-

    with:

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group
# — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow (it
# waits forever on a group its own caller holds).
#
# Agent code and the dmtools CLI are NOT tied to the workflow pin: they
# resolve from RELEASES at run time by repo variables (bump = repo-settings
# edit, zero workflow changes):
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools (Java) CLI release tag ('latest' default)
name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main (same pin as ai-teammate.yml).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # #687: whose login is "the machine" — pr_approved arming and the
      # auto-rework rules fire only on PRs authored by this login
      # (.dmtools/config.js machineAuthor carries the same value).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the required
      # protection check itself. your branch protection requires
      # exactly these contexts; keep the names in sync with the ruleset.
      validation-checks: '["test"]'
      # sm_github.json validation rules dispatch THIS repo's PR CI
      # (unit-tests.yml) on PR heads — without it the required context
      # never appears and approved PRs stall BLOCKED.
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified); it rides
      # this INPUT instead.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time. EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares.
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token).
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic merge bot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-latest
      # your PR CI — the bot's workflow-run fallback reads its runs when
      # a head carries no check runs.
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Why this repo needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet
# repos — the kicker re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule +
# every non-main push, so the state machine keeps moving even when the
# machine-sm cron is dropped.
#
# Event-driven wake-up: validation verdicts arrive as CI
# conclusions (your PR CI workflow);
# reacting to them closes the gap — latch/merge happens within seconds of
# the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: ajaxspace/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: 'CI'
      # The required protection context is the single `test` job named
      # "Java unit tests" ("Protect main" ruleset — see unit-tests.yml).
      required_contexts: 'test'

## Requirements

- Flutter mobile project (Android + iOS targets), clean default structure

- **Remember me**: persist the session locally so the user stays signed in across app restarts
- **Google sign-in** integration (credential save / autofill where the platform supports it)
- **Apple sign-in** integration (per Apple guidelines)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` pass
- [ ] `flutter test` passes (at least a widget test for the login page)
- [ ] Login page renders on Android and iOS
- [ ] Google and Apple sign-in wired, with saved credentials / autofill where supported
